newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stalls after hitting six-month low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stalls after hitting six-month low.

text.p: IPE Brent futures held at modestly lower levels after stalling when they hit new six-month lows on bearish technicals, warmer weather and more Iraqi barrels ear-marked for the U.S.

"I think it held due to the fact that traders were reluctant to sell it and force New York to open 30 to 40 cents lower," said one floor broker. "Initially stops were hit and took us down to the $19.81 level early."
At 1246 GMT, April Brent was 21 cents lower at $19.87 a barrel after dropping early to $19.81, the lowest level on the spot contract since last August.
Support was pegged at $19.75, where the bottom of a six-week downtrend channel crosses, and then at $19.70, another previous low from last August, brokers said. Deeper support was seen at $19.50.
Traders said IPE Brent was following NYMEX crude lower after the United Nations' sanctions committee on Thursday approved deeper discounts for Iraqi crude sales to the U.S.

The discount was taking into account deteriorating U.S. sour crude prices that were partly blamed on refinery maintenance turnarounds, traders said, adding that the Iraqi crude was finding little interest in the saturated domestic market.
March gas oil traded $2.75 lower at $170.75 a tonne after hitting a seven-month, spot contract low of $169.75.

Forecasts for much-above normal weather in the Northeast U.S. and warmer temperatures in Northwest Europe punctuated what traders said was an end to the winter heating oil season amid replenished supplies.
